result.title: Scale-Recursive Rectified Flows for Few-Step Precipitation Ensembles
result.summary: Fine-resolution precipitation estimates support flood risk assessment and water management, but coarse satellite products cannot resolve rainfall within each grid cell. Generative models address this ambiguity by producing ensembles of plausible high-resolution rainfall fields. Among these models, rectified flows generate samples by iteratively transforming random noise into rainfall fields. Reducing the number of sampling steps accelerates generation but can make ensemble members too similar, understating uncertainty. We propose a scale-recursive rectified flow that generates broad patterns before local details and guides sampling-step allocation by comparing ensemble variability with prediction error across spatial scales. Validation scores and rainfall power spectra constrain the allocation to avoid excessive amplification. In satellite-to-radar downscaling over the contiguous United States, our analysis identified broad rainfall patterns as the main source of insufficient ensemble variability under reduced sampling budgets. Allocating more steps to the coarse flow improved probabilistic accuracy and rain detection across training seeds at fixed architecture and computational cost. The proposed model also achieved better probabilistic accuracy with shorter sampling time than a nonrecursive flow using more steps.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出尺度递归的 rectified flow，用于卫星到雷达的降水降尺度集成生成：先生成粗尺度大范围降雨格局，再补充局部细节，并依据各空间尺度上集成变异性与预测误差的比较来分配采样步数。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心概念「按尺度分解状态并按不确定性分配计算步数」可能启发 LVR 中的动态计算预算与 STOP 决策：可核查多尺度潜在状态的分层生成与步数分配是否能类比到视觉推理的粗细证据获取顺序。
